target_customer: AI operators and data center developers needing fast, large scale power and compute capacity
problem: AI compute is limited by access to power and by local opposition and slow permitting on land.
business_model: Shipyard-built floating compute barges of 75 to 100 MW paired with power vessels, sold or leased as compute campuses
product_category: Offshore data center and power infrastructure

founders.name: Dimitris Koutentakis
prior_employers: Amazon (MILP optimization for electric fleet charging)
education: MIT, undergraduate, MEng EECS, MS Mechanical Engineering and MBA (MIT Sloan)
founders.background_notes: Connections to the Greek shipping industry per YC page.

education: MSc Chemical Engineering, Ghent University (valedictorian of engineering school)
founders.background_notes: No employers listed on YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Marine nuclear reactors need regulatory and engineering breakthroughs; the company starts gas-first with a 2028 pilot target and a nuclear swap years later.

defensibility.rationale: Shipyard standardization and any licenses obtained would be hard to copy, but nothing is built or licensed yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent had shipped a nuclear floating data center as of late 2026; coverage questions reliability and untested jurisdiction rules.

market_need_then: AI data center demand outstripped grid power and local siting in 2025 and 2026; the company cites community opposition on land.

identity.visual_style: Numbered sections, large headline statistics, small uppercase labels

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Tom's Hardware, DCD and a YC launch video feature; Demo Day roundups named it among startups VCs kept citing.

brand_strength.rationale: Name blends atom and marine and fits the idea; wide press coverage of the concept, but evidence is about the idea more than the brand.

outcome_analysis: Atomarine is a two person Summer 2026 company that attracted unusual press and a reported $19M seed after Demo Day. Its pitch is nuclear, but the first product is gas powered with a 2028 pilot target, so the central risk is regulatory and technical. No exit or failure has occurred; success factors are not assigned until deployment.
notes: The $19M seed is reported by DCD, Black Ridge Research and TradedVC (traded.co logged 2026-11-09); I could not open the DCD article (HTTP 403) and saw the details only in search snippets, and found no primary announcement. Lead investor attribution to Y Combinator is as reported and may be loose. Dealroom lists a $125k seed, which matches YC standard terms and is not recorded as a round. Headquarters conflicts (Boston vs Cambridge, MA). Reports differ on nuclear timing (2031 to 2032) and gas pilot (2028).
